instructions: Pat the chicken dry and cut it into 2-inch chunks. Season the chunks with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
In a bowl, stir the cornstarch with the garlic powder, 1/2 tsp of the paprika and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Toss the chicken in it, then shake off the extra.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the chicken in a single layer, 3 minutes per side, until golden. Transfer it to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the onion and garlic for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until the onion turns see-through. Add the remaining 1 tsp paprika and the thyme and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the wine, add the bay leaves and simmer for 3 minutes, until it smells less sharp and has reduced by about half.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Return the chicken to the pan in a single layer and turn each piece in the sauce.
Cover, turn the heat down to low and simmer for 10 minutes, shaking the pan now and then. The chicken is done at 165°F in the thickest piece, or when it's white all the way through with no pink.
Take the pan off the heat and remove the bay leaves. Sprinkle the parsley over and serve.
method_notes: Only one version of this dish by name was readable with full amounts (Spain on a Fork, 5.0 from 3 votes, so it leads as a fallback). It floured the chicken in wheat flour; here the coating is cornstarch so the dish stays gluten-free. Other pages (Spanish Sabores) agree on the pan-fried chicken in a tomato, onion and paprika sauce but could not be read, so nothing was compared. The list's rice or potatoes are not in the source, so none are added.
